prompt: Animate the supplied accepted Frogtown keyframe as an original two-dimensional exploration scene at a riparian planting pocket beside the concrete Los Angeles River. Keep exactly one unicorn, one albatross, one dog, and one cat with stable silhouettes and restrained neon markings. Give each animal a different, coherent action over five seconds: the dog investigates the path edge and returns attention to the group; the cat steps onto a low concrete rise; the albatross walks to moving plants and examines them with head and wing-edge motion; the unicorn turns toward changing water reflections and then back to the others. The group should remain socially connected and regroup around one small discovered river-edge detail. Keep the camera mostly fixed until body-driven motion is unmistakable. Preserve bold off-white and black fields, sparse cyan, chartreuse, magenta, yellow, and coral, tactile ink and paper texture, asymmetrical geometry, and generous negative space. No text and no audio.
negative_prompt: spike-shaped projection on any animal back
review_questions: Does each animal perform a distinct location-directed action?
Does body and environmental motion clearly exceed camera motion?
Does the scene retain concrete, path, water, and riparian Frogtown anchors?
Do the four animals remain recognizable and socially connected?
Does the final regrouping create a useful episode shot rather than a disconnected montage?
